title: The ordinary completed-coefficient quotient tensor is adjoint to inverse limit
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and any scheme W, with independent site and coefficient universes. With the fixed scalarReductionExtension, coefficientOrdinaryQuotient and coefficientSequenceRestriction of [def-trf-completion-unit-models], there is an OrdinaryModel l E W: an additive simultaneous tensor functor, natural level scalar-extension isomorphisms commuting with every strict quotient transition, an adjunction to ordinaryLimit with sectionwise unit x mapped to 1 tensor x, and a termwise-complex limit comparison whose degreewise projections are the actual inverse-limit projections. No derived coefficient calculus, derived adjunction comparison or Roos comparison is asserted.

source.place: 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, and sites-cohomology.tex 0941; coefficient specialization of canonical-model step 1.

proof.text: Use purSequenceOrdinaryFactorization to obtain its ordinary quotient projection O. Take its additive pullback as the tensor, its finite scalar-extension comparisons as the evaluation isomorphisms, and its recorded tensor_transition equations as the strict quotient compatibility. The extra constant-ring factorization data is not needed here.

Transport O.adjunction through O.limit to obtain an adjunction to ordinaryLimit. Apply O.transpose to O.adjunction.unit.app M. The inverse Hom correspondence sends this unit to the identity. Expanding the finite Hom correspondence and cancelling the inverse and forward tensor comparisons identifies the projected transported unit with the finite scalar adjunction unit. The fixed finite-unit normalization gives unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection 1 x; the unrestricted and scalar-reduction existence witnesses are definitionally the same construction.

Construct the cone of inverse-limit projections on each cochain complex of towers. Evaluation in each integer degree identifies this cone with the ordinary limit cone. HomologicalComplex.isLimitOfEval gives its universal property. The unique comparison with the chosen complex limit is natural, by equality after each projection, and has the required degreewise projection formula. Whisker this comparison with the coefficient restriction tower and assemble OrdinaryModel. No boundedness, flatness or nonzero-object hypothesis is used.
